cases.sentence: Авдотья Романовна была бледна; ___ ее дрожала в руке брата.
cases.translation: Avdotya Romanovna was pale; her hand was trembling in her brother's hand.
cases.explain: Рука is the grammatical subject of дрожала (was trembling), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Дуня, я этого ___ не желаю, а потому ты и должна, завтра же, при первом слове, Лужину отказать.
cases.translation: Dunya, I do not want this marriage, and so you must, tomorrow, at the first word, refuse Luzhin.
cases.explain: A negated transitive verb (не желаю) governs the genitive case for its object.

cases.sentence: Но я пойду к здешней ___, — настаивала Пульхерия Александровна, — я умолю ее, чтоб она дала мне и Дуне угол на эту ночь.
cases.translation: But I will go to the landlady here, insisted Pulkheria Alexandrovna, I will beg her to give me and Dunya a corner for this night.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) always governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Он слабо махнул Разумихину, чтобы прекратить целый ___ его бессвязных и горячих утешений.
cases.translation: He waved weakly at Razumikhin to stop the whole stream of his incoherent, fervent consolations.
cases.explain: Поток is the direct object of прекратить (to stop), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Он стоял с обеими ___, схватив их обеих за руки, уговаривая их и представляя им резоны.
cases.translation: He stood with both ladies, having grabbed both of them by the hands, persuading them and presenting reasons.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: В этом ___ просвечивалось сильное до страдания чувство, но в то же время было что-то неподвижное, даже как будто безумное.
cases.translation: In that gaze a feeling so intense it verged on suffering showed through, yet there was also something fixed, almost mad about it.
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating location governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Разумихин принял их обеих под руки и потащил с ___.
cases.translation: Razumikhin took them both by the arm and dragged them from the staircase.
cases.explain: The preposition с (from, away from) governs the genitive case.

reading.ru: Раскольников приподнялся и сел на диване.
reading.question: What did Raskolnikov do at the very start of the chapter?
options: He sat up on the sofa
reading.correct: He sat up on the sofa
reading.explain: The chapter opens with Raskolnikov raising himself and sitting up on the sofa.

reading.ru: Мать испугалась его взгляда.
reading.question: How did Pulkheria Alexandrovna react to her son's look?
options: She was frightened by his gaze
reading.correct: She was frightened by his gaze
reading.explain: The text states plainly that the mother was frightened by his gaze.

reading.ru: Авдотья Романовна была бледна; рука ее дрожала в руке брата.
reading.question: What physical detail is given about Dunya (Avdotya Romanovna) in this scene?
options: She was pale and her hand trembled in her brother's hand
reading.correct: She was pale and her hand trembled in her brother's hand
reading.explain: Avdotya Romanovna was pale, and her hand trembled in her brother's hand.

reading.ru: Ступайте домой… с ним, — проговорил он прерывистым голосом, указывая на Разумихина, — до завтра; завтра всё…
reading.question: What did Raskolnikov tell his mother and sister to do, pointing at Razumikhin?
options: Go home with him until tomorrow
reading.correct: Go home with him until tomorrow
reading.explain: He tells them, in a broken voice, to go home with him (Razumikhin) until tomorrow.

reading.ru: Я останусь при нем! — вскричал Разумихин, — ни на минуту его не покину
reading.question: What did Razumikhin vow to do regarding Raskolnikov?
options: Stay by his side and not leave him for a minute
reading.correct: Stay by his side and not leave him for a minute
reading.explain: Razumikhin cried that he would stay with him and not leave him even for a minute.

reading.ru: Пойдемте, маменька, хоть из комнаты выйдем на минуту, — шепнула испуганная Дуня, — мы его убиваем, это видно.
reading.question: Why did Dunya suggest they step out of the room for a moment?
options: Because their presence seemed to be distressing Raskolnikov badly
Because the room was too hot
reading.correct: Because their presence seemed to be distressing Raskolnikov badly
reading.explain: Frightened, Dunya whispers that they are killing him, it's clear, and suggests stepping out.

reading.ru: я этого брака не желаю, а потому ты и должна, завтра же, при первом слове, Лужину отказать, чтоб и духу его не пахло.
reading.question: What demand did Raskolnikov make regarding Dunya's engagement?
options: That she refuse Luzhin the very next day
That she wait a year before deciding
That she ask their mother's opinion first
reading.correct: That she refuse Luzhin the very next day
reading.explain: Raskolnikov insists that he does not want this marriage and that she must refuse Luzhin tomorrow, at the first opportunity.

reading.ru: В бреду? Нет… Ты выходишь за Лужина для меня. А я жертвы не принимаю.
reading.question: What reason did Raskolnikov give for opposing Dunya's marriage to Luzhin?
options: He believed she was marrying Luzhin as a sacrifice for his sake, which he refused to accept
He thought Luzhin was too poor
He wanted her to marry Razumikhin instead
He didn't believe Luzhin truly loved her
reading.correct: He believed she was marrying Luzhin as a sacrifice for his sake, which he refused to accept
reading.explain: He says she is marrying Luzhin for his sake, and declares that he does not accept such a sacrifice.

reading.ru: Бредит! — закричал хмельной Разумихин, — а то как бы он смел!
reading.question: How did the tipsy Razumikhin explain Raskolnikov's harsh words to the women?
options: He claimed Raskolnikov was delirious and didn't mean it
He blamed Luzhin for provoking Raskolnikov
reading.correct: He claimed Raskolnikov was delirious and didn't mean it
reading.explain: The drunken Razumikhin shouts that he is delirious, otherwise he would not dare say such things.

reading.ru: Слышишь, сестра, — повторил он вслед, собрав последние усилия, — я не в бреду; этот брак — подлость.
reading.question: What did Raskolnikov insist to his sister as she was leaving, despite Razumikhin's excuse?
options: That he was not delirious and the marriage was vile
That he was too tired to argue further
That he wanted to meet Luzhin himself
reading.correct: That he was not delirious and the marriage was vile
reading.explain: He insists, gathering his last strength, that he is not delirious and that this marriage is baseness (подлость).

reading.ru: Я ни за что не могу уйти! — шептала она Разумихину, чуть не в отчаянии, — я останусь здесь, где-нибудь… проводите Дуню.
reading.question: What did Pulkheria Alexandrovna insist on doing, almost in despair?
options: Staying near Raskolnikov while Razumikhin escorted Dunya
Taking Dunya straight back to their hometown
reading.correct: Staying near Raskolnikov while Razumikhin escorted Dunya
reading.explain: She whispers desperately that she cannot leave, that she will stay nearby, and asks him to escort Dunya.

reading.ru: Клянусь вам, — продолжал он полушепотом, уж на лестнице, — что давеча нас, меня и доктора, чуть не прибил!
reading.question: What did Razumikhin reveal to the women on the stairs about Raskolnikov's earlier behavior?
options: That he had nearly attacked Razumikhin and the doctor
That he had tried to run away
That he had confessed something shocking
That he had refused all medicine
reading.correct: That he had nearly attacked Razumikhin and the doctor
reading.explain: Razumikhin swears, half-whispering on the stairs, that Raskolnikov had nearly struck him and the doctor earlier.

reading.ru: Но я пойду к здешней хозяйке, — настаивала Пульхерия Александровна, — я умолю ее, чтоб она дала мне и Дуне угол на эту ночь. Я не могу оставить его так, не могу!
reading.question: What plan did Pulkheria Alexandrovna insist on regarding lodging for the night?
options: Begging the landlady to let her and Dunya stay somewhere in the building
Asking Zosimov to find them a room
reading.correct: Begging the landlady to let her and Dunya stay somewhere in the building
reading.explain: She insists she will go to the landlady here and beg her for a corner to spend the night, unable to leave her son.

reading.ru: Разумихин был в необыкновенном возбуждении.
reading.question: What was Razumikhin's emotional state as he walked the women down the stairs?
options: He was in an extraordinary state of excitement
He was falling asleep from drink
reading.correct: He was in an extraordinary state of excitement
reading.explain: The narrator states that Razumikhin was in an extraordinary state of excitement.

reading.ru: Невозможно к хозяйке, и вздор ужаснейший! — вскричал он, убеждая Пульхерию Александровну.
reading.question: What did Razumikhin say about Pulkheria Alexandrovna's plan to go to the landlady?
options: That it was impossible and absolute nonsense
That it was a wonderful idea
That the landlady would refuse anyway
That Dunya should go alone instead
reading.correct: That it was impossible and absolute nonsense
reading.explain: He exclaims that going to the landlady is impossible and the most terrible nonsense.

reading.ru: Пойдемте, маменька, — сказала Авдотья Романовна, — он верно так сделает, как обещает.
reading.question: What did Dunya say to persuade her mother to trust Razumikhin's plan?
options: That he would surely do as he promised
That they had no other choice
That Raskolnikov wanted them to leave
That the doctor had already agreed
reading.correct: That he would surely do as he promised
reading.explain: Dunya tells her mother to come along, trusting that he will certainly do as he promises.

reading.ru: Вот вы… вы… меня понимаете, потому что вы — ангел! — в восторге вскричал Разумихин.
reading.question: How did Razumikhin react to Dunya's trust in him?
options: He exclaimed in delight that she was an angel for understanding him
He asked her to repeat herself
reading.correct: He exclaimed in delight that she was an angel for understanding him
reading.explain: In rapture, Razumikhin cries out that she understands him because she is an angel.

reading.ru: И он стал на колени середи тротуара, к счастью, на этот раз пустынного.
reading.question: What dramatic gesture did Razumikhin make in the street?
options: He knelt down in the middle of the pavement
reading.correct: He knelt down in the middle of the pavement
reading.explain: He knelt down in the middle of the pavement, which was fortunately deserted at that moment.

reading.ru: Перестаньте, прошу вас, что вы делаете? — вскричала встревоженная до крайности Пульхерия Александровна.
reading.question: How did Pulkheria Alexandrovna react when Razumikhin knelt on the pavement?
options: She was extremely alarmed and told him to stop
reading.correct: She was extremely alarmed and told him to stop
reading.explain: Extremely alarmed, she cried out for him to stop, asking what he was doing.

reading.ru: Знаете ли, кого сюда пускают?
reading.question: What was Razumikhin outraged about regarding the women's lodgings?
options: The disreputable kind of people admitted to that lodging house
The high price of the rooms
reading.correct: The disreputable kind of people admitted to that lodging house
reading.explain: He angrily asks if they know what sort of people are let in there, criticizing Luzhin for putting them there.

reading.ru: Так, так… хоть я и не во всем с вами согласна, — серьезно прибавила Авдотья Романовна и тут же вскрикнула, до того больно на этот раз стиснул он ей руку.
reading.question: What happened physically to Dunya as Razumikhin spoke passionately?
options: He squeezed her hand so hard it hurt, making her cry out
She pulled her hand away calmly
reading.correct: He squeezed her hand so hard it hurt, making her cry out
reading.explain: As she agreed with him, he squeezed her hand so painfully that she cried out.

reading.ru: Ровно через двадцать минут по уходе Разумихина раздались два негромкие, но поспешные удара в дверь; он воротился.
reading.question: How soon after leaving did Razumikhin return with news?
reading.correct: Exactly twenty minutes later
reading.explain: Exactly twenty minutes after Razumikhin left, two quiet but hurried knocks sounded — he had returned.

reading.ru: Не войду, некогда! — заторопился он, когда отворили дверь, — спит во всю ивановскую, отлично, спокойно, и дай бог, чтобы часов десять проспал.
reading.question: What news did Razumikhin bring about Raskolnikov's condition?
options: That he was sleeping soundly and hopefully would sleep for ten hours
That he had woken up and left again
That he was calling for his mother
reading.correct: That he was sleeping soundly and hopefully would sleep for ten hours
reading.explain: Razumikhin reports that Raskolnikov is sleeping deeply and soundly, and hopefully will sleep about ten hours.

reading.ru: Авдотья Романовна была замечательно хороша собою — высокая, удивительно стройная, сильная, самоуверенная, что высказывалось во всяком жесте ее
reading.question: How is Dunya's appearance and demeanor described in this chapter?
options: Remarkably beautiful, tall, slender, strong, and self-assured
Plain and awkward in her movements
reading.correct: Remarkably beautiful, tall, slender, strong, and self-assured
reading.explain: The narrator describes her as remarkably good-looking — tall, wonderfully slender, strong, and self-confident.

reading.ru: Слушай, — сказал он Зосимову, — ты малый славный, но ты, кроме всех твоих скверных качеств, еще и потаскун, это я знаю, да еще из грязных.
reading.question: How did Razumikhin bluntly describe Zosimov near the end of the chapter?
options: A good fellow but also a womanizer, among his other bad qualities
reading.correct: A good fellow but also a womanizer, among his other bad qualities
reading.explain: Razumikhin tells Zosimov he is a fine fellow but, among his bad qualities, also a womanizer, and a low one at that.
